intended_object: The closed subspace L^p(α, m, μ; F) of L^p(α, m0, μ; F) for a sub-σ-algebra m: the classes in Lp that have an m-strongly measurable representative, viewed as a 𝕜-submodule. This is what the docstring and the module's use in building the conditional expectation describe.
explanation:
The carrier is `{f : Lp F p μ | AEStronglyMeasurable[m] f μ}`, i.e. the classes that are μ-a.e. equal to an m-strongly measurable function. This is the standard description of L^p(m) sitting inside L^p(m0), and it matches the docstring. The closure proofs (zero, addition, scalar multiplication) are routine.

**Degenerate cases.** No condition `m ≤ m0` is required, which is harmless. When m = m0, every element of Lp belongs to the subspace (`mem_lpMeas_self`), as it should.

**Scalar field.** The only special setting is `RCLike 𝕜`, which comes from the file-wide `variable` declaration. The scalar-multiplication step would also work over any normed field acting on F, so the definition could be stated more generally. But this is just the choice of which scalars give the submodule structure; the object itself does not change. Mathlib also provides the scalar-free version `lpMeasSubgroup`. RCLike is the setting of the surrounding conditional-expectation theory, which needs inner-product spaces over ℝ or ℂ. So this is not a real narrowing of the mathematical notion.

I did not find any other Mathlib definition of this subspace.
